summary: Broken down along the management and support categories of the APQC Process Classification Framework: finance (9.0) gives general accounting, billing and payables, planning and cost accounting, tax, and payroll; human capital (7.0) gives recruiting and workforce administration; procurement (4.2), projects (13.2), process management (13.1), knowledge and records (13.5) and risk and control (9.8, 11.0) give one capability each. Office tools, which APQC does not model, follow the UNSPSC software classes that O*NET carries (word processing, presentations, spreadsheets, email, calendars, conferencing). Leaves were cut where PMBOK, ISO 15489, COSO, XBRL and HR Open Standards draw distinctions, and ERP was dropped as a capability because it bundles these functions rather than adding one.

capabilities.name: General accounting and financial close
capabilities.definition: Given an organization's business transactions and chart of accounts, keep the double-entry ledger, reconcile it, close periods and produce financial statements.

crosswalk.label: Applied computing > Enterprise computing > Enterprise information systems > Enterprise resource planning

capabilities.notes: Was seed 'Accounting, bookkeeping and financial close; billing and invoicing'. Billing, receivables and payables split out as their own capability (APQC 9.2 and 9.6 are separate process groups from 9.3). Also absorbs the general-ledger and financials modules of the dropped ERP seed.

tasks.name: Double-entry ledger bookkeeping
tasks.definition: Given business transactions and a chart of accounts, post balanced journal entries and maintain account balances and a trial balance.
tasks.inputs: chart of accounts, source transactions, journal entries, fiscal calendar
tasks.outputs: posted ledger, account balances, trial balance, audit trail
onet_products: Pro Systems Client Write-Up System for Windows
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: given a transaction set and chart of accounts the correct balances and trial balance are deterministic
tasks.notes: Fund accounting (nonprofit and government) is a ledger variant with restricted-fund dimensions, kept here rather than as its own task.

tasks.name: Account and bank reconciliation
tasks.definition: Given ledger entries and an external statement, match items, identify differences and propose adjusting entries.
tasks.inputs: ledger detail, bank or subledger statements, matching rules
tasks.outputs: matched and unmatched items, reconciling differences, adjusting entries
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: synthetic ledger and statement pairs with known matches give precision and recall of matching

tasks.name: Period close and consolidation
tasks.definition: Given ledgers of several legal entities, translate currencies, eliminate intercompany balances and produce consolidated balances for the period.
tasks.inputs: entity trial balances, ownership structure, exchange rates, intercompany transactions
tasks.outputs: consolidated trial balance, eliminations, minority interest, close task status
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: consolidation rules (IFRS 10, ASC 810) applied to a synthetic group give a unique consolidated result

tasks.name: Financial statement preparation
tasks.definition: Given a closed trial balance and a reporting framework, produce the balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement and notes.
tasks.inputs: closed trial balance, account mapping to statement lines, reporting framework
tasks.outputs: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, notes
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: statements are deterministic from a mapped trial balance; the indirect cash-flow method is a good hard case

tasks.name: Structured financial report tagging
tasks.definition: Given financial statements, tag each fact with elements of a published reporting taxonomy and produce a valid machine-readable filing.
tasks.inputs: financial statements and notes, reporting taxonomy (US GAAP, IFRS)
tasks.outputs: inline XBRL instance document, validation results

crosswalk.label: eXtensible Business Reporting Language 2.1 and Inline XBRL

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: SEC filings with their XBRL tags form a large labeled corpus; XBRL conformance suites exist for validation
tasks.notes: eXtensible Business Reporting Language sits in the Development environment category in O*NET; listed here as the example because no other product string names the function.

tasks.name: Fixed asset depreciation
tasks.definition: Given a fixed-asset register and depreciation conventions, compute periodic book depreciation, disposals and net book values.
tasks.inputs: asset register, acquisition cost, useful life, method and convention, disposals
tasks.outputs: depreciation schedule, journal entries, net book value roll-forward
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: straight-line, declining-balance and conventions give exact expected schedules

tasks.name: Lease accounting
tasks.definition: Given lease contracts, compute right-of-use assets, lease liabilities and their amortization under the lease standard.
tasks.inputs: lease terms, payments, discount rate, options, modifications
tasks.outputs: right-of-use asset and liability schedules, journal entries, disclosures
tasks.benchmarkable: yes: ASC 842 and IFRS 16 calculations are deterministic for given terms

capabilities.name: Billing, receivables and payables

crosswalk.label: Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements

crosswalk.label: Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements

tasks.notes: Invoice data capture from images is in enterprise.documents.form_extraction.

capabilities.name: Budgeting, forecasting and cost accounting
capabilities.definition: Given historical financials, operating drivers and cost data, produce budgets, forecasts and the cost of products, jobs and activities.

crosswalk.label: Financial planning and analysis / corporate performance management

capabilities.notes: New capability, carved out of the ERP and accounting seeds. APQC treats planning and management accounting (9.1) as a separate process group; the O*NET budgeting, Hyperion and cost-accounting products had no home in the seeds. Statistical forecasting methods belong to science; this node is the planning workflow around them.

tasks.name: Operating budget preparation

tasks.name: Driver-based financial forecasting

tasks.inputs: actuals, driver series (volumes, prices, headcount), driver-to-account logic
tasks.outputs: rolling forecast by account and period, scenario comparisons
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: forecast accuracy can be scored against held-out actuals of public companies

tasks.name: Activity-based cost allocation

tasks.inputs: cost pools, activity definitions, driver volumes, allocation rules
tasks.outputs: unit costs, cost by product or customer, profitability

tasks.name: Job and project costing

tasks.outputs: job cost reports, committed and actual cost, cost to complete, margin

crosswalk.scheme: PMI PMBOK Guide 6th ed. knowledge area
crosswalk.label: Project Cost Management

tasks.benchmarkable: yes: cost accumulation and overhead absorption are deterministic
tasks.notes: Earned-value control of a project schedule is enterprise.projects.earned_value; this task is the accounting side.

tasks.name: Cash flow forecasting
tasks.definition: Given bank balances, receivable and payable schedules and planned flows, project daily to monthly cash positions and funding needs.
tasks.inputs: bank balances, open receivables and payables, payroll and debt schedules
tasks.outputs: projected cash position by account and period, funding gaps
tasks.benchmarkable: partly: deterministic roll-forward is testable; forecast accuracy needs held-out bank data

open_questions: ERP was dropped as a capability: it bundles accounting, procurement, HR and payroll rather than adding a function, and its 266 O*NET products are mostly industry suites. Its products are cited on the functional tasks instead. If the editor wants a node for suite integration (shared master data across modules), it would be enterprise.master_data and overlap computing's data management.

Sixteen capabilities exceeds the 6 to 14 target. The finance split (four capabilities plus payroll) follows APQC 9.x process groups, and office tools are split into authoring, spreadsheets and communication on the lead's instruction. Merging receivables_payables back into accounting would bring it to fifteen.

No-code tables (Airtable, QuickBase) are placed in enterprise.process_workflow while desktop databases (Microsoft Access, FileMaker Pro) are handed to computing. The line between end-user record tools and databases should be confirmed.
Employee shift scheduling is placed in enterprise.payroll_time. Health may claim nurse staffing and move claims crew scheduling; the general rostering problem should have one owner.

APQC codes are from memory of the cross-industry PCF version 7; version 8 renumbered some process groups. Codes are given only at category and process-group level where I am confident, and left empty below that.
